decisions: D1 (owner-only list, PRD §9 Q1): OWNER_ONLY_ACTIONS = platform_update_task_status and platform_update_task when the status is done or cancelled; platform_assign_tool_to_agent; platform_unassign_tool_from_agent; platform_update_agent; platform_update_system_setting; platform_create_mission; platform_approve_mission; platform_cancel_mission; platform_publish_blog_post; platform_submit_social_post; every Composio send/publish action. The kit's reading of the PRD; the owner trims the list before launch by editing this line.

D7 (the baseline): the eval runner and set live OUTSIDE the repo (~/.automatos-analyst/auto-eval/, gold data). The loop NEVER runs it and never writes it; the baseline (arms A and C, about $6) is the owner's run. US-007 in this wave is the docs page and the CI-visible contract only.
D8 (receipts source): receipts are built from the in-process ToolExecutionTracker.outcomes at save time, never from tool_execution_logs (it stores parameter names only, no result, no chat id).

D9 (one PR per wave): story commits end with ' [skip ci]'; the runner pushes them as a backup to a branch that has NO pull request, so test.yml does not run (since #993 it runs on pull_request and push-to-main only). The runner opens the wave's draft PR once, when the build is COMPLETE, which starts the wave's single CI run; the acceptance gate reads that run.

D10 (the families): action_claims / document_claims / shop_and_team_claims are FROZEN in this wave (no new pattern; a test pins their counts) and deleted in Wave 2 US-012 only after the receipts rule is proven.
project: PRD-256 Auto, receipts not narration — Wave 1: receipts, honesty, gates, tool contracts, the instrument
description: Wave 1 of PRD-256 (docs/PRDS/PRD-256-AUTO-RECEIPTS-GATES-CONTRACTS.md, seeded onto the branch by the runner). US-001..US-007 in priority order: the receipts part (built from the tool tracker, shown above the text, saved, DELEGATE turns too); one honesty rule driven by receipts (the families frozen); memory takes receipts; the owner's click on owner-only actions through the existing grant card; done needs an artifact; strict first-class schemas for Auto's write actions and 'a refused write is reported refused'; the docs page for the instrument. No migration. The decisions above answer the PRD's §9 for this wave and are binding. Browser checks and every eval run are the owner's (ownerTest below); the loop never runs a browser, a server, a test suite or the eval, and never marks those DONE. Diff base for every check: `bash scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd256w1.sh --print-base`.
ownerTest: Before or beside the launch: the baseline eval, arms A (today's Gemini) and C (Sonnet 5), on today's build: `cd ~/Development/Automatos-AI-Platform/automatos-ai && python3 ~/.automatos-analyst/auto-eval/replay.py --arm gemini-0.7 --yes` then `--arm sonnet-5 --yes` (about $6). Its two lines in runs/results.md are the 'before'.

US-001 in the browser (1440 px and 390 px) on the local stack after merge: a turn that only stored a memory shows 'No actions on the board' above the text; a turn that made a ticket shows its number and a link; reload shows the same block; a turn with no calls shows 'No actions in this turn.'

US-004 in the browser: 'Cancel #<a card in review>' from chat shows the approval card naming the card and 'cancel'; nothing moves until Approve; after Approve the card is Cancelled and the note is signed by you.
After merge: the post-wave eval, arms A and C again; the delta against the baseline on the four rates is the wave's exit criterion (PRD §10).
Both editions: the same checks on the local stack and, after deploy, on SaaS.

userStories.title: The owner's click on owner-only actions
userStories.description: As an owner, I want approvals, cancellations, agent and tool changes, settings and anything that publishes or sends to wait for my click when they come from chat, so Auto's words alone can never act or sign for me.
acceptanceCriteria: A new small module `orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/owner_only.py` holds `OWNER_ONLY_ACTIONS` exactly as Decision D1 lists them, with the status condition for the two task actions, and `is_owner_only(action_name, params) -> bool`.

In `PlatformExecutor.execute` (modules/tools/discovery/platform_executor.py), when `caller_context.driving_user_id` is set and `is_owner_only(...)` is true, the executor returns the confirmation ask through `tool_grants.attach_ask_grant` exactly as a requires_confirmation action does today; the ask names the subject (the card by number) and the verb; the owner's click resumes the call through the existing grant path (consume_tool_grant). Agent runs, playbook steps and heartbeats (no driving user) are unchanged.
The note a card gets from a chat-driven move is written only when the owner clicked, and signed by the user who clicked (services/board_consent.actor_from_user_id); never on Auto's call alone.

follows_the_owner.py no longer imports or applies APPROVE, CANCEL or GO_AHEAD from owner_turn.py (those paths and their helpers are deleted, not shimmed); 'the card the owner named is the card acted on' (a card number never reaches a non-card write tool; no copy instead of the named card) stays with its tests.
'Cancel #0422' from chat produces an ask naming #0422 and 'cancel'; nothing moves until the click; the policy plane (AUTOMATOS_POLICY_PLANE) is NOT required for this gate; both editions.
The hierarchy gate (orchestrator/scripts/check_hierarchy_gate.py) passes: no ActionDefinition moves outside registry.register.

userStories.title: Tool contracts for Auto's writes
userStories.description: As an owner, I want Auto's writes to land first time, so a failed call never has the chance to be reported as done.
acceptanceCriteria: The write actions are PROMOTED and PINNED so `ActionRegistry.to_first_class_schemas` ships them as their own tools outside the dispatcher's enum: platform_create_task, platform_update_task, platform_update_task_status, platform_assign_task, platform_create_mission, platform_execute_playbook, platform_schedule_playbook, platform_create_social_post, platform_store_memory, platform_get_task, platform_query_data. Mechanism: the registry's promoted set plus `TOOL_ROUTING_PROMOTION_PINS` (an existing key; names added, no new key).

Each promoted schema is strict: every required field listed in `required`; `status` an enum of the board's own words; `params` typed as an object with its fields named; no free-text catch-all. platform_execute still decodes a JSON-string `params` (F181); the promoted tools never need it.
The ATOM lane ships the promoted tools beside the dispatcher (service.py's ATOM branch calls the same first-class builder; the change is a call, not new code in service.py).

After a refused write, the loop's nudge (modules/tools/execution/nudges.py) says: a reply after a refused write states the write was refused and why; it never reports it done. The Auto system prompt (modules/context/sections or services/brief_facts.AUTO_OWNER_RULES, whichever the rules block reads) carries the same one rule.
`check_hierarchy_gate.py` passes; the promoted actions keep their permission levels; the `[tool-shadow]` surface log still reports shipped versus would-be-first-class counts.

Tests: `orchestrator/tests/test_prd256_tool_contracts.py`: a schema test per promoted tool (required fields, enums, params as object); a loop test with a refused write and a fake model that claims success, asserting the nudge text; a test that the ATOM surface includes the promoted tools.
